Riya said to me, “I am happy to see you.”

options.text: Riya told me that she is happy to see you.
Riya told me that she was happy to see you.
Riya told me that she was happy to see me.
Riya told me that she is happy to see me.

questions.solution:

__
 
• The given sentence is in a **direct speech**.
 
• The given speech is in **Simple present tense**.
 
• When the reporting verb of direct speech is in** **the** past tense, **all the present tenses are changed to the corresponding **past tense **in** indirect speech.**
 
• The basic rules for changing or converting **direct speech** into **indirect speech**:
 
 
• Change** "am"** in reporting speech into **"was"**.
 
• Replace comma (,) and inverted commas (" ") with the conjunction **"that"**.
 
• The first person in the reported speech **"I"** changes according to the subject of the reporting clause **"She"**.
 
 
 
• Hence, the correct answer is: **"Riya told me that she was happy to see me."**

Therefore, the correct answer is **"Option 3"**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• In **Indirect speech**, tenses do not change if the words used within the quotes (‘’) talk of a **habitual action** or **universal truth.**
 
• For Example: 
 
 
• **Direct**: He said, ‘We cannot live without air’.
 
• **Indirect**: He said that we cannot live without air.
